title: Roasted Butternut Squash Soup with Sage and Pumpkin Seeds
summary: Roasted butternut squash is blended with a soft onion and carrot base into a smooth, golden soup, finished with cream, crisp sage leaves and toasted pumpkin seeds.

ingredients.item: butternut squash (1 large), peeled, seeded and cut into 3 cm chunks (about 1 kg prepared)
fine sea salt or table salt
double cream, plus 2 tbsp to swirl

steps.title: Roast the squash
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C). Toss the squash with the oil and a pinch of the salt on the lined tin and roast for 35-40 min, turning once, until soft and browned at the edges. Roasting caramelises the natural sugars, giving a deeper, nuttier flavour than boiling.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Meanwhile, melt the butter in the pot over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 8 min until soft. Add the garlic for 1 min, just until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer together
steps.text: Add the roasted squash, broth, water, remaining salt and pepper. Bring to the boil and simmer for 10 min so the flavours meld and the vegetables are completely tender.

steps.title: Blend smooth
steps.text: Blend until very smooth. With an upright blender, fill it no more than half full and hold the lid down with a towel, as hot soup builds pressure. Stir in the 80 ml cream and lemon juice and reheat until steaming and just bubbling, thinning with water if needed.

steps.title: Crisp the topping
steps.text: Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium heat and fry the sage leaves for 30 s until crisp, then lift out. Toast the pumpkin seeds in the same pan for 2-3 min until they pop; the sage-flavoured oil coats the seeds as they toast.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Ladle the soup into bowls, swirl in the remaining cream and scatter with the seeds and sage.

tips: A common mistake is crowding the squash on the tin; spread it out so it roasts and browns instead of steaming.
Pull the sage leaves out as soon as they turn crisp, as they burn within seconds.
Add the lemon juice at the end to lift the sweetness of the squash.
Thin the soup with a little water rather than more cream to keep it light.
storage: Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat until boiling hot (74°C), stirring often.
